title: Soul Searchers Looking for a Purpose

sense.text:
To soul search is to look within: the examination of your conscience, your motives and your values. What motivates you, what causes you to do what you do, and what is valuable to you: your family, the Lord, your job, that new car you just bought? And purpose is intention: what was God’s intention when he created us? This class is for those within the body and for those without it, because a lot of our people outside the body are looking for purpose. They see us out there saying the white man is the devil, which he is, and we ain’t sugarcoating it, he is Satan; but the Bible is bigger than that. Our people battle depression and mental health issues, and that stuff is real. If you do not strengthen and examine your mental health, you will be out here crazy.

The Lord says “thou, Israel, art my servant, Jacob whom I have chosen”, and then he gets specific: “the seed of Abraham my friend.” That seed came from Abraham and went to Isaac, because Isaac is Jacob’s father. He did not say Esau, though Esau came from Isaac as well. He did not say Ishmael, Abraham’s first son by Hagar, the handmaid of his wife. He did not mention those two nations. He mentioned only one nation, the nation of Israel, and that’s you: the so-called black, Hispanic and Native Americans. You have a purpose.

“Yet now hear, O Jacob my servant”: he is talking to you. “And Israel, whom I have chosen”: there he goes again. What are these Christians reading? God didn’t choose all nations, and Christ didn’t come to contradict this. If Christ came and now all nations are chosen, why would the Lord have this written? Christ said no jot or tittle shall in no wise pass from the law, and Isaiah is the law; the whole book is the law.

“Thus saith the Lord that made thee, and formed thee from the womb”: he formed thee from the womb. “Which will help thee”: he is going to help you; that’s a promise, and God don’t break his promise. “Fear not, O Jacob, my servant”: he tells you not to be afraid. “And thou, Jesurun, whom I have chosen”: Jesurun is just another name for Israel.

Over and over throughout the scriptures the Lord says what his intention is for the Israelites: who he chose and why he chose them.

The beginning of Isaiah 63 is straight vengeance: Isaiah saw Christ coming with a vengeance, destroying our enemies. Then the chapter takes a turn: “I will mention the lovingkindnesses of the Lord, and the praises of the Lord, according to all that the Lord hath bestowed on us, and the great goodness toward the house of Israel.” Great goodness toward who? The house of Israel. That goodness the Lord has extended, and is going to continue to extend, to the house of Israel. Don’t let anybody fool you. He bestowed it “according to his mercies, and according to the multitude of his lovingkindnesses.”

A sister on Clubhouse asked what the point of this life is: you’re just going to die, people are going to do you wrong. But where do you go when you die? We think when death comes it’s over. No, that’s just the beginning. If you die before Christ returns and you are not keeping his commandments, you are literally just waiting to be judged. But if you die in Christ keeping the commandments, you are going to be in paradise, and when his kingdom comes you are going to sit on the throne with him. Whoever asks what the point of this life is doesn’t understand their purpose, and doesn’t understand that there is a judgment after you die. That is what we have to make clear to our people, and what we are supposed to be living by.

“For he said, Surely they are my people”: what’s that word? Surely. So why are we walking around with our head hanging down? Why do we let people at our job make us feel insignificant? Why you let that no good negro tell you you ain’t no good? Some of you kids go to school and they mock you: keep your head high and carry yourself with grace. Brothers, we are the kings of this earth, and it’s time for us to understand that our sisters are the princesses of this earth. We should not be living like the world; we are better than that.

“Children that will not lie: so he was their Saviour.” He is going to save the nation of Israel; that’s a promise. Look how much we have been through as a nation and are still going through. The Bishops travel all over the world. Some of y’all never been to a third world country, and it’s real bad. You complain about the air condition; they have never felt an air condition. In the islands, like Grenada, they have single units in individual rooms; you better open a window or a door and get some breeze up in here. What we take for granted, our people in those countries have never experienced, but the Lord still says “Surely they are my people.”

“In all their affliction he was afflicted”: the Lord sees what they are doing to you, and it does piss him off. Everything we have gone through, the Lord himself was afflicted by it. Some people say God ain’t doing nothing, he don’t feel no type of way. A woman called God narcissistic: why does he think we should serve him? Maybe because your brain works and the blood is flowing through your veins right now. Your heart ain’t stopped; you have no disease that keeps you from walking or moving like some people out here; you can see and talk, and your body works like it’s supposed to. You have the power to get up and look at your children, the power even to have children. That is the reason you should be serving God. God ain’t narcissistic; he wants you to give him the respect he has given you. The Lord respected us enough to create us the greatest nation on earth.

“And the angel of his presence saved them: in his love and in his pity he redeemed them; and he bare them, and carried them all the days of old.” The Lord went and got our people out of Egypt. Egypt was the greatest nation on earth at that time, with the greatest military, all the wealth and all the wisdom, and the Lord destroyed that nation little by little, and for his final finale killed all their firstborn sons and let his children come out. At the very beginning of Exodus they were trying to kill our sons; then they took the brick and mortar from us and made us go out and get the straw, get the materials ourselves, and still meet the quota. Imagine your job sending you up on a roof to put up shingles with no shingles and no drill, and still wanting that roof up by sundown. That’s what they did to us. But by the end of us being in Egypt we came out of that thing shining. The Lord said give them all your gold, and we went in loin cloths getting our backs whipped and walked out of that thing bling blinging. That’s what your God does for you, and he ain’t forgot about us. He is going to do it again.

precepts.why:
Somebody says God don’t respect nobody, God is no respecter of persons. Read it: “And God looked upon the children of Israel, and God had respect unto them.” God had respect unto them, and God has respect unto us. He looked at what he made and said, that looks good right there, I respect that.

When the Bible says no respect of persons, it means that among us, brothers, rank don’t matter. If one is a king and the other an hourly worker at a job, the Lord will judge the king for his evil the same way he will judge the worker. Anybody can get it: King David got it, King Saul got it, King Solomon got it; all the forefathers that were great men still got some judgment at one point in their life. So there is no respect of persons with God, but as far as the children of Israel are concerned, God had respect unto them. That is the God who in all their affliction was afflicted.

sense.text:
“Happy art thou, O Israel: who is like unto thee”: he is asking a question he already knows the answer to. Who looks like these sisters? Who is more graceful and lively than these women? Who is stronger, more masculine, smarter and more intelligent than these men? There are none, and they know it. That’s why they went out of their way to destroy your mind, so you would never find your purpose, and it’s working on millions of us. Millions on this earth are searching for their purpose, and it’s our job, brothers, to go wake them up.

“O people saved by the Lord”: why does he keep saying he is going to save the nation of Israel? This is the book of Deuteronomy, and this is prophecy. “The shield of thy help, and who is the sword of thy excellency”: the Lord is the sword of our excellency. “And thine enemies shall be found liars unto thee; and thou shalt tread upon their high places.” To tread upon their high places is that we are going to destroy the governments and the high leaders ruling in the high places right now, in the last days, and then walk in their wealth and in their glory.

Thine enemies shall be found liars: everything the Bible said would happen has happened. Did we not come on slave ships? Did the Lord not say that at night we would wish it were morning and in the morning wish it were night? Do we not fear when no man pursueth? Then why would these promises not happen? They are going to happen.

Their own books bear it out. Who’s Who in Philadelphia, by Charles Fred White, says the Negro learns from history that Hannibal, the world’s greatest general, was of Ethiopian blood; but Hannibal was an Israelite from the tribe of Asher. It says King Solomon, the wise man of our Bible, proudly acknowledged that he was black; that the Jews were mixed with African breed, and our foremothers, Jacob’s wives, were of another nation, because Jacob is the father of the Israelites; and that Jesus Christ himself was as much a negro as some of the race you persecute. We didn’t write this. These are historical data, and these white folks wrote it, so don’t get mad at us; get mad at them.

Another book, The Negro and the Jews, written by an old white woman, says all the native inhabitants of the land of Israel and that region were nonwhite, and that when Spain expelled its Jews in 1492 many went to Africa, and it seems probable some were brought later to America as slaves. You blacks in America today are descendants of those that were in Spain, expelled to Cape Verde and other places, and brought to Brazil, to the Caribbean islands, and eventually to the United States, and she knows it. She writes that the spirituals never sing of African rivers but of the Jordan or the Red Sea; not of African chiefs or kings but of David or Moses. Could we read and write in the English language when we got here? No. So when did we start thinking about Moses and David? We already knew them, because Moses and David were our ancestors and we already had our records. When they got to the west coast of Africa they found the records of the Jews among us. There was a kingdom in Ghana called the kingdom of Judah, and a whole portion of West Africa was called Negroland; we have the maps. They have always known who we were; my people just haven’t learned it yet.

precepts.why:
This is walking in their wealth and treading upon their high places. “And they shall build the old wastes, they shall raise up the former desolations, and they shall repair the waste cities, the desolations of many generations.” Think of the dilapidated, rundown, third world looking houses in our communities, in Jackson, Mississippi, in certain poor cities in North Carolina: a tarp up on the roof because they can’t afford a new roof, pots on the floor when the rain comes through, dumping the pots outside and running back in to fill them again. Black folks, Israelites, Hispanics are living like that in the greatest country on earth.

“And strangers shall stand and feed your flocks, and the sons of the alien shall be your plowmen and your vinedressers.” They told you the so-called Hispanics are illegal aliens; the Bible says no, they are the aliens, and they are going to work for us. They think they are working now; they are going to work twice as hard then.

“But ye shall be named the Priests of the Lord: men shall call you the Ministers of our God”: you Israelites. “Ye shall eat the riches of the Gentiles”, because their riches are our riches; the money they have, they stole from us. “And in their glory shall ye boast yourselves”: we are going to say, this was your diamond, get on back out there; all them rings on your hand and bracelets, get on away from around here. That’s what they get for messing with God’s chosen.

“For your shame ye shall have double”: since we went through shame, the Lord says I’m going to give you double. “Therefore in their land they shall possess the double: everlasting joy shall be unto them.”

“And their seed shall be known among the Gentiles, and their offspring among the people.” When your children walk through the palace, pass by the fields, fly past (because we are going to be flying), they are going to say, let me bow down; I know you’re nine years old, but you the man. In slavery, when a little Edomite boy said I’m going to tell my daddy you did such and such to me, a grown man would drop to his knees and cry, please don’t tell Massa, he going to kill me, he going to rape my wife. Their children had us in fear. Now the Bible says when our children walk through, they will be known.

“All that see them shall acknowledge them, that they are the seed which the Lord hath blessed.” When they see our children they are going to bow; it is going to be undeniable that God is with us in that day. So why are you walking around thinking you ain’t got no purpose, when all these amazing promises are in the Bible and you know they are going to come to pass?

sense.text: Another history book says the black Jews had an advantage over the African tribes. Before going any further, that is what the scripture asks: “What advantage then hath the Jew? or what profit is there of circumcision?”

“Much every way”: every way. “Chiefly, because that unto them were committed the oracles of God.” God’s oracles were committed to the Jews; the Jews had the wisdom and understanding of God’s laws, statutes and commandments. That’s what that means, and the book is on point.

The book says the black Jews carried their culture, history, laws and written records with them. Our history is Deuteronomy, Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers, the Kings, Samuel, Isaiah. Because we had the commandments, the history and the laws, we had a higher social organization: we were not hanging from trees, wearing loin cloths and banging on our chest like monkeys in West Africa. We have always been an industrious, intelligent people. They broke us when they got us; they had to beat it out of us to get a man to lay down on the bottom of a ship, and God had to remove the spirit from us.

Because of the stability of that culture, the Jews were not absorbed into the native population; the Jews absorbed some of the native tribes. In their states were found kings, princes, governors, generals, judges, architects, engineers, doctors, historians, mathematicians, jewelers, masons, carpenters, goldsmiths, blacksmiths and agriculturalists. That’s everything you need to establish a society: education, health, government, building, and making weapons, because we did have an army. We had it all, so don’t let them fool you and tell you you ain’t never been great.

We have to teach this all day, every day, to our people, because they don’t know who they are. Over a million of our ancestors rest at the bottom of the Atlantic. More than 12,000 ships made over 40,000 voyages: they went back and forth and grabbed our ancestors and brought them to this side of the world. That’s how you was born here. That is why the Lord sent us here, to wake up and teach this history and why this happened to us.

“The Lord shall bring thee into Egypt again with ships.” The Lord prophesied that he would bring us into slavery again on ships. “And there ye shall be sold unto your enemies for bondmen and bondwomen, and no man shall buy you.” First it says you’re sold; then it says no man shall buy you. That means no man shall redeem us. Who is going to redeem us? Christ.

People on the street will try to confuse you with this: wait a minute, didn’t it just say you gonna be sold, and then it say no man gonna buy you? Them urban apologists take the NIV to say you should offer yourself to be sold and no man will buy you. That’s a misinterpretation, a mistranslation, and they do that to confuse you, because the Israelites are rising up. The Bible said we would go into slavery on ships, and that’s what we just saw.

All those carpenters, doctors, blacksmiths, goldsmiths, language interpreters, kings, princes, governors and princesses were stuffed on the bottom of a ship. You can go inside the ship at a museum and see how tight it is, but you still can’t imagine the fear: you don’t know where you going, you ain’t never left your homeland, you see your mama thrown overboard, your father die right there because of the feces stacked up so high, sickness and disease, people throwing up everywhere because they ain’t never been on the ocean before. All that happened to us. Why? Because we the children of Israel and we sinned against our God.

Those were a great people on those boats, the children of God. We weren’t no dumb people. We had all the skill set to raise up this country for the white man: we built the White House, we built all the different structures. He didn’t do that on his own. We did that, and he knew we could do it.

You walk around here thinking you ain’t got no purpose, but you the Israelites, and even in tumultuous times, hard times, we’ve always risen to be great, because God chose us.

“This people have I formed for myself.” Who is this people? God said this people right here that you looking at, this people have God formed for himself.

“They shall shew forth my praise.” That’s what you see the men doing on the streets now, and what you see the sisters doing now when they wear their dresses and their hair wraps, when they taking care of their children; when you see the men marching through the streets, we showing forth God’s praise. We was in the gangs, we was doing drugs, brothers was adulterers, some brothers was in prison, but not no more. Now we walking as the army of God, changing our lives, showing forth God’s purpose, and we going to show forth God’s praise on this earth.

precepts.why:
Start at verse one: “But now thus saith the Lord that created thee, O Jacob, and he that formed thee, O Israel, Fear not: for I have redeemed thee, I have called thee by thy name; thou art mine.” The people God formed for himself in verse 21 is Jacob, Israel.

Hear what God said. You sit up here saying I’m going to let this drug run my life, I’m going to let this evil demon run my life, I’m going to let these people tell me my significance and my importance. No: God said “thou art mine.” You belong to me. That’s how the women feel about their kids: somebody try to take them and it’s no, you can’t have them, that’s my baby; you can play with him a little bit, but go on back to Daddy, that’s mine right there. That’s how God feels about us.

Even though we’ve been afflicted, he is going through affliction too, watching us be afflicted, but he can’t break his word. We got to do our part. The only way God is going to redeem us and bring us out of this captivity is when we start doing our part. He said I’mma punish you if you sin against me; we keep sinning, so he keeps punishing us; but when we turn from the sin, he going to turn from that punishment. It’s that simple. God’s ways are equal; our ways are unequal.

Skip down to verse 10: “Ye are my witnesses, saith the Lord.” Not the Jehovah’s Witnesses. Charles T Russell started the Jehovah’s Witnesses, and that’s who you following, but the Bible says the Israelites are God’s witnesses: we are the ones that witnessed his true power and his word.

“And my servant whom I have chosen”: Israel is God’s servant whom he has chosen. Then back to verse 21: this people have I formed for myself.

sense.text:
What is your purpose, you soul searching? “Let us hear the conclusion of the whole matter: Fear God, and keep his commandments: for this is the whole duty of man.” Brothers, sisters, that’s it. That’s our purpose, what he created us for: to fear him and to keep his commandments.

But a lot of us have not yet found our true purpose because we still in the midst of sin. We still got hatred, we ain’t getting along in our marriages, husbands not doing what they supposed to do, wives not holding up their end of the bargain. It’s happening in Israel right now. We got to change, we got to grow, we got to mature, all of us. That’s what the Bible is about. Our purpose is to be better than we were yesterday, to serve God better than we did the day before.

Whatever is impeding your progress in serving the Lord, you got to get rid of it, you got to work on it: your health, a lying tongue, an adulterous, whorish spirit, hatred in your heart for your sister, your brother, your spouse. It’s your duty, because your duty is to fear God and keep his commandments.

Why? “For God shall bring every work into judgment.” There’s going to be a judgment day, “with every secret thing”, even the things you think no one knows about, “whether it be good, or whether it be evil.” God knows it, God sees it.

That’s where the fear comes from: oh shoot, the Lord sees what I’m doing right now, let me stop doing this. That’s where integrity comes from: ain’t nobody here to see it, but I know God’s watching, so I’m going to do the right thing. Some do the right thing with people around, for vain glory, so somebody says real good job, I saw you give that food to them little children. But if the cameras weren’t around, would you still do it?

A lot of brothers are behind the scenes in the body, in the stewardship program, and sisters behind the scenes doing different things, not seen in the forefront like the officers, deacons and Bishops, and you may feel insignificant. But are you doing it for what man sees, or for what the Lord sees? All you men are going to have your opportunity to lead. We all started as brothers, soldiers, then became officers, and the Israelites are going to be in the millions; somebody has to lead all them people. Some of you that are 20s now will be captains later; some that are 10s now will be 80s later. It’s up to you to fulfill your purpose and prove yourself. Don’t get antsy about where you at. Some people walk slower than others. Keep your hand to the plow, and never give up, never give in.

Let’s talk about purpose. “Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee.” You all know what takes place: the sperm cell reaches the egg and activates it, the child is conceived and grows in the woman’s womb, and after nine months the body, the brain, the heart and the organs are fully developed and the baby comes. But before that even happened, while that spirit was in the heavens and the Lord sent that spirit through the father, the Lord already knew him. It was a decision made in heaven for you to be here.

Then you come down here and do drugs, kill yourself, let depression and anxiety overtake you, but that’s not what you was created for. A man carries millions upon millions of sperm cells every single day, but the Lord found it fit to make sure you were the one that reached the egg first. That’s not something to play with.

“And before thou camest forth out of the womb I sanctified thee”: before you came out of the womb he had already sanctified you. “And I ordained thee a prophet unto the nations.” When that sperm cell was on its way to the egg, the Lord said this one right here is going to be a prophet, and he ordained it while the mother was walking around six, seven, eight months pregnant, going through the morning sickness and the pain. The Lord was helping her through it, saying you about to bring forth a prophet.

That’s what the Lord said to Zacharias about John the Baptist, what he told Jeremiah right here, and what he told Mary about Christ. These men he is bringing back on this earth have a purpose, and it’s not just them. All of us have a purpose.

People out here struggling don’t understand they got a purpose. They built a box for safely abandoning newborn babies: you place the infant inside, take the orange bag of resources, shut the door and walk away, and it locks; your baby may be crying in there and you can’t get the baby out until the police show up, and they might take you to jail for abandoning the child. The white man is the devil; he going to give you every opportunity to break God’s commandments. They say the baby is only in there a minute and twenty-some seconds, but how many things can happen to make that baby suffocate in there? These folks hate us. They know we got a purpose, and as many of us as they can control and destroy, they’re going to do it.

The CDC counted 625,000 abortions in 2021 in the states it had data for, and the Guttmacher Institute’s count for 2020 was higher still: in one year almost a million babies were aborted, and less than 1% of those are from rape, though they always try to say that. Economic factors, social economic status, children out here having sex that shouldn’t be having sex and getting pregnant: nonetheless it’s wicked as hell. You don’t know that child’s purpose, what the Lord had for that child, and you eliminated that spirit from coming on this earth.

precepts.why:
That’s why the Lord judges our people: because of the innocent blood on our hands. “These six things doth the Lord hate: yea, seven are an abomination unto him: A proud look, a lying tongue, and hands that shed innocent blood.”

That child is innocent. That child ain’t came on the earth yet, but you took that child before it ever made it. Out of those 900,000, a large majority are Black and Hispanic, guaranteed, because they push the option of abortion harder in our communities. That’s in the Bible: hands that shed innocent blood.

Remember the Lord said he had a purpose for Jeremiah. “And now, brother, behold what glory; and see the people that cometh from the east: Unto whom I will give for leaders, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob”, and on through the prophets, Amos and Joel, Jonas, Nahum, Zachary and Malachy, “which is called also an angel of the Lord.”

So Abraham is back on the earth today. Abraham came back on this earth through the sperm of a man in captivity. These men, the fathers and the prophets, are going to be the leaders of the people that come from the east, the same way the Lord had already ordained Jeremiah before he was formed in the belly.

“For thy help will I send my servants”: the Lord said he is going to send Isaiah, and he is going to send Jeremiah, “after whose counsel I have sanctified and prepared for thee twelve trees laden with divers fruits.”

The Lord told Jeremiah, I sanctified thee a prophet. That means Jeremiah wasn’t just sanctified as a prophet when he lived as Jeremiah; he was sanctified as a prophet in today’s time, as he lives today. So you don’t know which one of these kids may be Jeremiah, but you going to go to the clinic and kill that baby. You don’t know what you doing.

And it’s not only the sisters: there are men that contribute to abortion too, that leave money on the nightstand and say go take care of that. There are wicked, no good men out there that kill babies too, so we ain’t just blaming the sisters. But we go so hard on the sisters because y’all are the ones that end up with the child, and you go through a lot with that child.

Jeremiah is back on the earth, but Jeremiah ain’t going to know he’s Jeremiah until a certain point in his life when he gets woken up, and even when he wakes up he’s still not going to know that he is the prophet Jeremiah.

“And thou, even thyself, shalt discontinue from thine heritage that I gave thee”: he is talking to Jeremiah, telling him that in the future he is going to discontinue from his heritage. “And I will cause thee to serve thine enemies in the land which thou knowest not”: he told Jeremiah he would go through slavery and be oppressed. “For ye have kindled a fire in mine anger, which shall burn for ever.”

So Jeremiah is back on the earth today, going through trials and tribulations and systemic oppression; he could have been incarcerated; he may not even have woken up yet, and right now he is possibly going through pure hell. What if he gives up and gives in to drugs, goes out and starts knocking brothers and sisters off, killing and robbing people, and completely wastes his purpose and his existence? He can’t do it. The Bible prophesied that he is going to be back on the earth in these last days teaching.

And you may be Jeremiah. Why you thinking about giving up, doing drugs, committing adultery? Don’t waste your purpose. Your purpose is not to be here to fulfill the lust of your flesh; your purpose is to be here to fulfill God’s will for you.

sense.text:
You are given an assignment. The Lord is bringing you into the counsel that happened in the heavens; he gave that understanding to our forefather Ezra, and Ezra wrote it down: “And now when I prepared the world, which was not yet made, even for them to dwell in that now live, no man spake against me.”

What is that telling you? The people that now live, those spirits were in heaven with God before they came to the earth, through the sperm of a man, through the womb of a woman. Nobody spoke against God up there.

“For then every one obeyed”: in your spiritual body, your angelic body, your celestial body, you can’t sin against God. You ain’t never going to not serve God in that body, because you weren’t created to do that. You only sin when you come down here in this flesh; it’s hard in this flesh, you got to fight.

“But now the manners of them which are created in this world that is made are corrupted by a perpetual seed, and by a law which is unsearchable rid themselves.” The angels keep God’s commandments; the angels obey God. It wasn’t until we got down here that we rid ourselves of that law. We stopped following God’s laws when we came into the flesh, so the Lord had to punish us and bring us down.

precepts.why: “In the year that king Uzziah died I saw also the Lord sitting upon a throne, high and lifted up, and his train filled the temple.” Isaiah saw a vision of the Lord sitting on his throne in heaven. Isaiah is not in heaven with God; he is seeing a vision, seeing himself in the spiritual realm, in that counsel where the world was prepared for them that now live.

“Also I heard the voice of the Lord, saying, Whom shall I send, and who will go for us? Then said I, Here am I; send me.” Isaiah sees himself in the heavens saying, send me, I’ll go.

We just read in 2 Esdras that the Lord said he’s going to send Isaiah back, and we just read another prophecy in 2 Esdras that before we came to this earth the Lord had already given us our assignment. So Isaiah stood up and said, I’ll go down there, send me. He said that in the heavens. You think Isaiah got time to be down here wasting his time like he ain’t got no purpose? You may be Isaiah, because the Bible did confirm that he’s here in the last days teaching, or going to be teaching. You ain’t got no time to play.

“And he said, Go, and tell this people, Hear ye indeed, but understand not; and see ye indeed, but perceive not.” He gave him an assignment, what he wanted him to do. That is the assignment given before the spirit ever came down into the flesh.

sense.text: “The Lord hath called me from the womb; from the bowels of my mother hath he made mention of my name.” From the bowels of your mother he made mention of you. He said, this one is going to be a prophet; this one right here is going to be a daughter of Sarah; this one right here is going to be a princess; that one right there is going to be an evangelist; that one is going to be an apostle. He already ordained what you are supposed to be. You don’t have time to waste this purpose.

precepts.why:
“And now, saith the Lord that formed me from the womb to be his servant”: what were you formed from the womb to do? To be his servant, “to bring Jacob again to him.” It’s your job to bring Jacob again to God. That’s why the Lord is sending Bishop to Papua New Guinea, why the Lord is sending these brothers over to Germany and wherever else, to teach, to bring them back. “Though Israel be not gathered, yet shall I be glorious in the eyes of the Lord, and my God shall be my strength.”

“It is a light thing that thou shouldest be my servant to raise up the tribes of Jacob, and to restore the preserved of Israel”: restore them, because of what they went through in Jeremiah 17:4. They lost themselves, they lost their heritage, they discontinued. The Lord said, now it’s your job to go resurrect them, restore them. You men have significance; you sisters have a significance.

“I will also give thee for a light to the Gentiles”: that’s the northern kingdom, and our brothers and sisters that speak these other languages and live in Gentile customs. “That thou mayest be my salvation unto the end of the earth.” That prophecy is being fulfilled right before your eyes. God is literally making all these scriptures we’ve been reading today come to pass, and you don’t even realize it, because you’re so caught up and consumed in your day-to-day life, so stuck in your own trials and tribulations, you ain’t paying attention to this mighty work God is doing on this earth. We close to the end. This ain’t no time to play no games, zero games.

sense.text:
“Where there is no vision, the people perish”: when people don’t have a vision, they will perish, like those young men in Mississippi. Someone like that only lives in the immediate present; they don’t live in the future, they don’t have no vision at all, they’re not even thinking. They haven’t been taught their purpose.

I hate to say it, but there’s a possibility one or two of those young men could die within the next couple of months. That video got a million views; somebody is going to see them on there talking about how dangerous they are, and wait till they see them out at the store with their grandma. Those are small towns, fifteen hundred, sixteen hundred people; you are going to cross paths with somebody or their family member. This is real.

precepts.why: “For as he thinketh in his heart, so is he.” As you think in your mind, so are you. If you think you’re only good enough to chase this money, only good enough to be a rapper or an entertainer or a social media influencer, if that’s all your mind is on, if your mind ain’t on God, then that’s what you’re going to become; that’s what you’re going to strive for. Only thinking about women, and so on and so forth. That’s what our people are in.

“He raiseth up the poor out of the dust, and lifteth up the beggar from the dunghill, to set them among princes, and to make them inherit the throne of glory: for the pillars of the earth are the Lord’s, and he hath set the world upon them.”

We got to go and raise these young men up, these young women up. The Lord prophesied that he is going to raise them out of the dunghill and set them among princes, but we got to be the ones that fulfill our purpose, to go show them theirs. That’s what the Lord called us to do.

sense.text:
Your thoughts are important. Thoughts create feelings, feelings create behavior, behavior creates thoughts, and it’s just a cycle: whatever you’re thinking is what you’re going to feel, your feelings become your behavior, how you act out, and your behavior develops more thoughts, round and round like a revolving door until you completely destroy yourself. That’s basically what the scripture is saying. They came up with that cognitive behavior theory, but the Bible been told you that. Christ already told you: “out of the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts.” The thoughts are evil; you have to correct those thoughts. Adultery starts in the heart, and adultery becomes an action.

This is for brothers and sisters that are in this truth too. You’re not exempt because you’re in the truth already; that don’t mean nothing. We got brothers and sisters in the truth in the midst of all kind of wickedness, and when we find that out, they got to be removed from the body. Adultery is real, and people are out here committing it right now. There are people that just committed adultery that will walk into the congregation; people that will go to camp with their brothers in the midst of adultery and come home and lay with their husband. We’ve seen this a lot lately; every spring and summer you see a lot of fornication going on, a lot of adultery. It ain’t worth it. That’s not your purpose.

Now you say, God showed me. A pastor said he told his wife, while she was still with her ex-husband, that she was going to be his wife: God showed it to me. And she left her husband and got with him. You think she just divorced him and then they started a relationship? No, she was already messing with him.
“Thefts, covetousness”: that’s seeing what somebody else got, seeing him blinging, seeing the car. “Lasciviousness”: strong sexual desires. Then “an evil eye, blasphemy, pride, foolishness”.
“All these evil things come from within, and defile the man.” It begins in the heart, in the thoughts, and comes out as the action that defiles the man.

precepts.why:
It’s not your purpose to sleep with another man’s wife, or another woman’s husband. That’s not what you were put here for, to get yours. “For this is the will of God, even your sanctification, that ye should abstain from fornication.” What does the Bible say you’re supposed to do? Abstain from fornication: abstinence.

“That every one of you should know how to possess his vessel in sanctification and honour.” Why? Because you have a purpose. You’re supposed to possess your vessel in sanctification and honour, and walk with integrity. Somebody tries to holler at you, you let them know: I’m married, it is what it is. Let it be known; let them know you stand for something.

Because if you leave that door open, especially to a no good negro, he’ll knock on that door every day: good morning beautiful, I see you changed your hair. He’ll drop that nugget and leave. And them work husbands, and the sister on the job: I can’t reach that up there, you so tall and strong, look at them shoulders. My wife don’t tell me my shoulders look good, and you put a little flex into it.

You don’t realize Satan is messing with you, trying to see what way he can get in. You’ll have real issues going on up front, financially, sickness, death in the family, and in the background Satan is working on you, because he’s got that sister trying to holler at you every day and that dude trying to holler at you at the job every day. Something bad happens up front, and you fall into the arms of that dude or the arms of that woman. You’re supposed to be walking around keeping your body in sanctification and honour.

sense.text:
Write your goals down: for the congregation, for your life, for your spiritual walk, for your financial walk, and fight to reach them goals by the end of 2024. Whatever you don’t meet, you can examine yourself and say why: I was slothful, I didn’t work hard enough in school, I didn’t fight for that promotion, I didn’t read my four chapters a day. I didn’t do it because I wasn’t disciplined enough. That’s what it’s about.

When you don’t know your purpose, every little obstacle popping your way is a big deal: oh it’s so cold, oh it’s so hot, oh it’s so early, oh God this happened. You can never stay on a straight and narrow focused path; you too busy worried about what’s on the left and what’s on the right, because you’ve lost your focus.

That goes back to Joshua: “This book of the law shall not depart out of thy mouth; but thou shalt meditate therein day and night”, like the picture of the Lord standing with you as you meditate in the scriptures. “That thou mayest observe to do according to all that is written therein: for then thou shalt make thy way prosperous”: because you got a focus, you got a goal, you meditate on the scriptures, you know what your purpose is, so then you become prosperous.

That don’t mean ain’t no obstacles going to pop up in the way. Some obstacles are going to pop up, but you’re going to overcome those obstacles, “and then thou shalt have good success.”

precepts.why: Your purpose drives you. It gives you energy, it gives you the spirit to endure. “He that getteth wisdom loveth his own soul”: when you get wisdom you love your own soul. “He that keepeth understanding shall find good”: and you’re going to find good, because you know your purpose. Wisdom is going to elevate you, take you to that next level.

sense.text:
Your body reacts to your thoughts, to the point where you can make yourself sick. Sickness don’t just come because you caught something at the job or the workplace; there are self-inflicted wounds that you give yourself, and a lot of them are psychological. Your brain don’t react the way it’s supposed to react when you allow it to go into depression.

Esau’s created different therapies and stuff to try to help you come up out of depression. Esau is always going to throw his therapies in there, because he wants to make his money: that’s how he makes his money, he capitalizes off people’s thoughts and people’s mental illnesses. But the Bible tells you: “Give not over thy mind to heaviness”: don’t give over your mind to heaviness, depression.

“And afflict not thyself in thine own counsel”: don’t say, well, I ain’t no good, I’ll never be good, I’ll always be like this, I’ll never be a prophet, I’ll never be a teacher, I’ll never reach my goals, I’ll never finish school. You can’t do that. You got to push, you got to fight, you got to be determined, you can’t give up.

It’s going to get hard. It’s hard to lose weight; it ain’t easy to go to the gym every single day, but you got to push. Thirty days is how you develop a habit (some people say 90, some say 60, I say 30). Go to the gym consistently every day of the week, besides the Sabbath and any high holy days, and your body starts to crave it: I got to build on this momentum. If I miss three, four days in a row I feel horrible, and when I go back it’s hard: damn man, I was lifting this two weeks ago and now it’s a struggle, because I missed so much time. You have to push yourself.

It ain’t easy to stay committed to education either. Some of you work a full-time job, you’re a parent, you’re in this truth and you’re in school. But you got to say, look, I got a purpose, I got a goal, I got to meet it. You got to remove that heaviness from your mind, that doubt from your mind.
“The gladness of the heart is the life of man, and the joyfulness of a man prolongeth his days”: why? Because you have a healthy heart, which is your mind.

“Love thine own soul”: the same thing just read in the Proverbs, love your own soul. “And comfort thy heart, remove sorrow far from thee: for sorrow hath killed many”: a lot of people done died from sorrow, because their brain ain’t working like it’s supposed to.

“And there is no profit therein”: there’s no profit in sitting around sad and sick all the time. You’re doing that because you don’t have a purpose, or at least you don’t know your purpose. The Bible is giving us clear instructions on how to deal with these things.

precepts.why:
That’s Satan on your brain, causing you to think like that. If you were meditating in the scriptures and you believed the scriptures, you would put the thoughts Satan is giving you to the side. “Submit yourselves therefore to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you.” The devil comes with them evil thoughts, having you thinking them evil things, like the picture of all these demons around you trying to pull you in every direction. The Bible says resist the devil and he will flee.

How do you resist him? By standing strong in his word and understanding your purpose: that you’re an Israelite, put on this earth to serve God and to serve God’s people.

“Draw nigh to God, and he will draw nigh to you. Cleanse your hands, ye sinners; and purify your hearts, ye double minded.” It’s time to stop being double-minded. It’s already been proven: as read earlier, our enemies shall be found liars unto us, meaning they can’t lie to us no more and tell us we’re not the Israelites. We got too much evidence; the truth is out here now. So you know who you are; now it’s time to get yourself together.

sense.text: You also got to find your purpose in this truth. “Know ye not, that to whom ye yield yourselves servants to obey, his servants ye are to whom ye obey; whether of sin unto death, or of obedience unto righteousness?” You become the servant of whom you obey. If you serve God, you’re God’s servant; but if you serve Satan, you’re Satan’s servant.

precepts.why:
“Let not sin therefore reign in your mortal body”: don’t let sin overcome you and reign, rule, “that ye should obey it in the lusts thereof.”

Think of the images of the thoughts of the mind. If this is all on your mind, it’s going to run your life, bro; it’s going to run your life, sister. If money is the only thing you think about, guess what you do: you get your body up for it, you’ll cheat God’s people for it, you’ll steal from God’s people for it. That’s what happened to the one who called himself a smart Christian: he was smart enough to get his dumbass put in jail for stealing.

Same thing with pornography. You know it’s wrong when you’re watching it, because you’re worried about somebody catching you. If I got to look over my shoulder to see if somebody’s going to catch me, about 100% of the time I shouldn’t be doing it. These things are all in the heart. Some brothers among us cannot stop thinking about vagina; it’s the only thing on their mind all day, because it comes out of their speech. Even in the church, lusting: that’s how it be in a Christian church.

So don’t let sin reign, that you obey it in the lust thereof.

“Neither yield ye your members as instruments of unrighteousness unto sin”: don’t allow your members, your body parts, to be used for unrighteousness, like prostitution, like stealing. Don’t use your brain to think and come up with evil ways to cheat people out of money.

“But yield yourselves unto God, as those that are alive from the dead”: meaning you understand your purpose. “And your members as instruments of righteousness unto God”: you wait until you marry, and then you use your members according to what the Bible says, to please your husband, to please your wife, to bring forth children. Now you can use your members, because you did it the right way.

Even your brain: use it to help the ministry, to help the body grow. You may be good with finances; help with accounting. Use your hands to build for the congregation, to hook up wiring. Come up with creative ways for social media. Use that stuff for positivity, to help God’s ministry, not for sin.

sense.text: “But thou hast fully known my doctrine, manner of life, purpose”: Paul said you know my doctrine, my manner of life, meaning how I live, the example I set for you, and my purpose. “Faith, longsuffering, charity, patience”: Paul said you’ve seen all these things. When I come around I will show you these things; I will live a certain way in front of you so that you can learn, and so that you can follow that same thing.
Paul endured “Persecutions, afflictions, which came unto me at Antioch, at Iconium, at Lystra; what persecutions I endured: but out of them all the Lord delivered me.”

“Yea, and all that will live godly in Christ Jesus shall suffer persecution.” You’re going to suffer persecution; you’re going to have to be tried, God got to try you. Don’t think that just because you’re in the truth God is not going to allow you to go through trial and tribulation. You’re going to have to go through some things.

But in going through these things you’re growing, you’re getting better, you’re getting stronger, you’re adding strength to your armor. At the end of the day, that’s your purpose, that’s your calling. Every last one of us got issues, things inside of us that need to be purged from us. It’s up to you to examine it, to see yourself: soul search.

Some of you may still be dwelling on your past; some of you feel a certain type of way based off some things you did before you came into this truth; and some of you may be involved in some things that you know you need to repent from. Watch what the Bible says: “Therefore if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature”. “Old things are passed away”: you’re not who you used to be, you’re different now. “Behold, all things are become new.”

Now a man finding his purpose in this truth, and a woman finding her purpose in the truth. First, the man.

“The prophets that have been before me and before thee of old prophesied both against many countries”: the prophets always prophesy against many countries, “and against great kingdoms, of war, and of evil, and of pestilence.” That’s our job, like the images of the prophets marching: to go out and teach against these things and put your life on the line for this. That’s your purpose, bro. That’s why you got breath in your lungs: to do this work, the work of the Lord. We are supposed to prophesy against many countries, against great kingdoms, of war and of evil and of pestilence.

precepts.why:
“And though the Lord give you the bread of adversity, and the water of affliction, yet shall not thy teachers be removed into a corner any more”: we’re not going to be moved into a corner anymore. The people are going to see us out there doing the work, they’re going to see us teaching, they’re going to see us out there marching for Kendrick Johnson and our different brothers and sisters whose lives have been tragically taken from them by the enemy. “But thine eyes shall see thy teachers”.

Without social media, some of these churches and these Christian apologists, nobody would know them; they have no works outside of social media. But a person that don’t have a telephone or a cell phone: Bishop and them just went to Papua New Guinea, and half them folks ain’t got no cell phone. For some of them folks, that’s the first time they heard the Bible like that, or even seen somebody teach the Bible like that, and they say, how can I get in touch with y’all, what do I need to do? So that means we got to establish congregations over there to do the work.

sense.text: Listen up, brothers. “This is a true saying, If a man desire the office of a bishop, he desireth a good work.”

“A bishop then must be blameless”: you got to be blameless, bro. Blameless don’t just go into having a beard, having fringes and a border of blue. Blameless goes into: you tell a brother you’re going to call him back, you call him back. You see something out of order with your household, you correct it. Sometimes you set stuff in order not because it’s sin, but because it gives off the appearance that it’s okay: you say, I want my household to be an example; no, you can’t wear that, no, you can’t do that, because another brother or sister that’s weak in the faith will see it and think it’s okay. You don’t want nobody to be able to blame you or the ministry.

You shouldn’t be drinking and driving. If you’re going to have a little strong drink or a little wine, going over scriptures with the brothers, get somebody to drive for you, get your wife to drive you home. Be responsible, because if you get pulled over for a DUI and your face is plastered everywhere, that affects the ministry. If you get pulled over by the police and you’re in a mood that day because you had a bad day, you ain’t got no time to be going back and forth with that person, because then they pull out a gun and shoot you, or they arrest you and say he was resisting arrest, and then they show the body cam footage in court and you were acting a plum fool. We can’t help you in that situation; you’re wrong. Being blameless goes into a lot of different things. Brothers, you got to be blameless.

“The husband of one wife”: you can only have one wife. One wife; somebody tell these brothers. “Vigilant”: meaning aware of your surroundings. “Sober”: you can’t be drunk, you can’t be high, you got to have sober thoughts.

“Of good behaviour”: you ever see some brothers that’s just rude? You can’t be like that in this truth. At something like a men’s conference with 1,500 brothers, you can’t salute every single body, but you can still be polite and respectful: hey, how y’all doing, good to see you men. You can’t be arrogant, mean and disrespectful. And that goes for outside this truth too: on your job you got to be of good behavior. You can’t be cussing your boss out because he’s an Edomite. We’re supposed to be past that; the Lord said live peaceably with all men.

“Given to hospitality”: you got to be willing to open yourself up to help people. “Apt to teach”: I don’t understand brothers not wanting to teach; I love to teach. Always try to go to camp if you can, teach class, read for the leadership: always ready to teach.

“Not given to wine, no striker”: no laying your hands on folks. “Not greedy of filthy lucre”: not trying to solicit money from people. “But patient”: you got to be patient. “Not a brawler, not covetous”: you can’t be covetous.

“One that ruleth well his own house, having his children in subjection with all gravity”: having your children in subjection with all gravity is not just pulling the belt out and beating them. It’s giving them understanding. When you sit down with your children you got to teach them, brothers. You can’t just pull a belt out and whoop them every time they don’t understand something. You have to show them: hold up, sit down, I took that from you because of this; that happened because you violated this; daddy put this rule in place because of that.

Ain’t nothing wrong with explaining yourself. I ain’t going to do it every time, but I’ll explain myself one time: this is why we do this in this house, because the Bible says this, and this is how Daddy wants it done. It’s been explained, the law has been laid down; now if you violate that, that’s when the spanking comes, not the first time. It’s just like a job: how are you going to write me up when you never trained me on what I’m supposed to be doing? If you had told me, I would have done it. It’s the same way with the kids, brothers. Gravity means grave, to be serious: you have to show your children the seriousness of what they’re doing and what they’re violating, with patience coming into that.

“(For if a man know not how to rule his own house, how shall he take care of the church of God?)” You can’t pull your belt out and whoop the congregation. That’s a grown ass man, and he might be bigger than you. Some of the brothers come out of that life, and you get to talking crazy, they get to smacking you. So when you’re dealing with a brother or a sister in the congregation, you have to deal with them with gravity, but it still can be respectful: as long as you ain’t bucking and being irate, we can have a discussion, we can have a conversation.

That starts in your household, and then you bring that into the school, and you’re able to lead properly. When you become a leader, a lot of people are going to say a lot of things: people slander you, people lie on you, put your name in things you never said to a brother you never spoke to. Show me the evidence. That happens in leadership, so you have to be mindful as a leader of how you’re dealing.

“But if any provide not for his own, and specially for those of his own house, he hath denied the faith, and is worse than an infidel.” Brothers: the best job is no job, don’t nobody want to work, not for no devil at least. If you go out here and work for yourself, that’s cool, because that’s something you control and you can take the time off to do the work of the Lord. But some of us got to go to work, be there at a certain time, stay till a certain time, follow all the rules there; these people pay our paychecks, so when they call we got to go. At the end of the day you have to endure that for your family.

Work your regular job, maybe work on an education or a certification on the side, so you can eventually lead that job or start your own thing. Nothing wrong with that. But as long as you got kids and a wife and a house and a car note and all that, your ass got to work. You got to figure it out, brothers.

If your wife is a good wife, she’ll see you struggling and say, let me get something at home for now, I can bake cakes, have a little cake-baking business. My mom did that when her and my stepdaddy hit hard times: she can bake, she started a little LLC and was making a whole bunch of money, and when we needed it, that money came right on time. Ain’t nothing wrong with a wife helping her husband with something on the side. But at the end of the day the responsibility falls on us, brothers. We got to take care of our household. If you do not take care of your household, you’re worse than an infidel, meaning an unbeliever.

precepts.why:
This is your purpose: to be an example, to be blameless, to rule your own house, to teach your wife, to teach your children and guide them. “The chief thing for life is water, and bread, and clothing, and an house to cover shame.” You’re supposed to be providing the chief things in life for your family.

If your situation ain’t right and you don’t have the money for a down payment, you might have to rent for a while, a year, and live below your means so you can save money. But you have to establish that plan and give it to them: look, we’re going to stay in this apartment for two years, we’re not eating out, we ain’t doing no extra bowling and all that, we’re going to sacrifice for these two years. Here’s my plan: we’re going to save x amount of dollars a month, and according to my calculations in 24 months we’ll have enough for a down payment on a house; I’m going to work on my credit, you work on your credit, and we’re going to get it done. That’s what a man is supposed to do: provide a vision. Then your wife can help, and you’re working together.

There’s nothing wrong with renting, but eventually strive to get your own; put things in place to get your own, brothers. It’s better for it to be yours, because the one you rent from can come in there and say, to hell with y’all, get out of here. “Better is the life of a poor man in a mean cottage, than delicate fare in another man’s house.” You’re saving money because you’re living in somebody else’s house, and you want to get up out of there.

sense.text:
“Health and good estate of body are above all gold, and a strong body above infinite wealth.” A strong body above infinite wealth, brothers: you got to exercise, you got to eat right. The only way they’re going to get right is when we get right: when we start losing the weight and getting in shape, bulking up or leaning out, whatever it is, they’re going to get right.

Get rid of the junk food. A Dorito chip put up under a microscope shows little parasites and bugs; once they put that stuff in a bag they just leave it there, and it develops parasites and bacteria, and then you’re feeding it to your kids and wondering why your kid is acting a fool, why their brain ain’t working right. Be mindful of that: you got to eat right, and you got to teach your family to eat right.
“There is no riches above a sound body, and no joy above the joy of the heart.”
“Death is better than a bitter life or continual sickness.”

You got to teach your family how to eat. It is your job, brothers, to teach your family how to eat, so you can fulfill your purpose. “Eat, as it becometh a man, those things which are set before thee”: eat the way a man ought to eat.

“A very little is sufficient for a man well nurtured.” If you eat right, you don’t have to eat a lot. If you want to burn fat you have to eat protein; some people do the keto diet; you eat less, you move more, you exercise. Those are the ways to burn fat, to shed fat, and you can do it.

But you have to do it first, brothers, and then the sisters will get in line when they see your example. When you ain’t doing nothing and they see you ain’t doing nothing, they just fall right into that same rut. Every time in my life I’ve gained weight, my wife gained weight; every time in my life I’ve lost weight, she’s lost weight. We one flesh. She can’t sit down while you going to the gym every day; she’ll say, ‘I’m looking bad, let me go with you.’ That’s what ends up happening. They follow our lead.
Now let’s deal with the sisters: what is a woman’s purpose? “It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him an help meet for him.” She was made to be a help meet for the man.

The Lord God caused a deep sleep to fall upon Adam, took one of his ribs, and of that rib “made he a woman, and brought her unto the man.” Adam said, “This is now bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh: she shall be called Woman, because she was taken out of Man.”

She was taken out of man. Sisters, y’all was made for us; that’s why you was created. You wasn’t created to be by yourself or to be independent. You was created for us, created to help us, to be our help meet, our pillar of rest.

precepts.why:
So any woman that says ‘I don’t need a man’, or is disrespectful to her man, you know that woman don’t know her purpose. “He that getteth a wife beginneth a possession”: when a man gets a wife he begins a possession, and he’s supposed to take care of that possession. She is “a help like unto himself, and a pillar of rest.”

Sisters, y’all supposed to be our pillar of rest. When we come home you supposed to sense that we done had a hard day. My demeanor when I come through the door tells you what kind of day I had, and that’s supposed to make you say, ‘Hey kids, y’all go upstairs, leave daddy alone for a minute. All praise to the Most High, let me make sure my husband is fed, let me make sure his stuff is in order.’ If I’m getting ready to travel, going to Blitz, you supposed to make sure my backpack is ready, because you believe in this truth and you believe in me: ‘Let me make sure my lord got what he need, because he going to go save God’s people, he going to go teach God’s people.’

You supposed to be a help meet when we struggle, when we down. Men don’t get into all that emotional venting like them dudes on social media. If I’m feeling some type of way I’m going to talk to my brother, and he going to tell me, ‘Suck it up, man, you ain’t the only one going through something. Stand up on your feet, stand up manfully.’ Sometimes you need that brother to tell you to shut up. But the sisters are supposed to sense the emotional stress your man deals with and make things easier for him, make sure he got what he need. That is a help meet.

sense.text:
“The aged women likewise, that they be in behaviour as becometh holiness, not false accusers, not given to much wine, teachers of good things.” A woman is supposed to be a teacher of good things. She’s supposed to have behaviour as becometh holiness.

It’s not holy to be out here twerking. It’s not holy to wear them long fingernails. It’s not holy to wear them rugs, or whatever them things is. Sisters in the truth that’ll wear that: don’t do it, sis. If your eyes are always red because of what you got irritating them, you might want to take them out. That glue y’all put right there gives you all kind of infections; women’s eyes swelled shut from it. It’s not meant to be on your eyes like that.
The aged women are to “teach the young women to be sober, to love their husbands, to love their children.” You supposed to be teaching the young women to be sober.

See that part where it says “discreet, chaste, keepers at home”? You know that new term they be saying, ‘We outside. I’m outside.’ No. I don’t want you outside, I want you inside. Go and make sure my house is good, make sure the kids is good, then teach these other sisters how to do the same.

precepts.why:
A keeper at home is the righteous woman. “Who can find a virtuous woman? for her price is far above rubies.” See how much y’all is worth. When we say don’t listen to black women, we talking about the evil sisters out here, the evil sisters that prophesy out of their own heart. But these righteous women, these women getting themselves right with God, we listening to them. If Abigail was here and in the spirit, we would listen to her; John the Baptist’s mama, Dorcas, Priscilla, these righteous women, we listen to them. This righteous, virtuous woman is worth more than rubies.

“The heart of her husband doth safely trust in her, so that he shall have no need of spoil.” Why does the heart of her husband safely trust in her? Because she at home handling her business. She not out and about in the streets all the time, running around, just wanting to be seen like some of these women do. She knows her purpose, and her purpose is to serve her husband.

“But the younger widows refuse: for when they have begun to wax wanton against Christ, they will marry; having damnation, because they have cast off their first faith.” Watch this: “And withal they learn to be idle, wandering about from house to house”, always in everybody’s business. “And not only idle, but tattlers also and busybodies, speaking things which they ought not.”

That’s why she is supposed to be busy doing the work of the Most High, busy taking care of her lord’s household, because when she’s not, she’s bouncing from house to house to house. It’s going on up in here, it’s going on in Raleigh; it goes on in every school, in Grenada, in Jackson, Mississippi, in New York. In every school sisters be sitting on the phone gossiping. A Deacon taught a class on that about two weeks ago, about gossip, about shutting your black lips. That is the behaviour as becometh holiness: sisters know they can’t call you with drama, because you ain’t going to listen to it. Next thing you know your phone starts ringing a lot less, because everybody realizes you ain’t going for it. That’s how it’s supposed to be; that’s the reputation you want to have in this truth.

“I will therefore that the younger women marry, bear children, guide the house, give none occasion to the adversary to speak reproachfully.” They waiting for one of you sisters to do something crazy so they can come at us and say, ‘Y’all women ain’t as righteous as y’all say. I seen her at the club the other day with them fringes on her clothes.’ Same as with the brothers: ‘I seen some guy with no fringes on and his beard cut; I thought y’all said a man supposed to have a beard, supposed to have fringes.’ They ain’t just watching us, they watching the sisters too. So you got to make sure you walking in your purpose, moving in the right spirit.

“For some are already turned aside after Satan.” There are some sisters right now in the congregations that are in the midst of wickedness, and we don’t know it, and they have not yet told us. We pray there’s nobody here, but we know it’s happening around the country and around the world, in the various schools: some have already turned aside after Satan.

sense.text: Fulfilling your purpose. “All things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose.” You going through trial and tribulation, but you keeping God’s commandments: you just keep on fighting through the struggle. Don’t never give up, because you was called according to his purpose, and all things are going to work together for you.

“For whom he did foreknow, he also did predestinate”: he foreknew you, and he predestinated you to be where you are today, “to be conformed to the image of his Son”, that we may walk like his Son, “that he might be the firstborn among many brethren.”

That is Christ’s death, burial and resurrection. Christ resurrected and got the angelic new body, and we going to resurrect and get that new body too.

precepts.why:
“Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who hath blessed us with all spiritual blessings in heavenly places in Christ.” Remember, earlier we went to 2 Esdras 9, where he gave us an assignment: I already told you what I got planned for you.

“According as he hath chosen us in him before the foundation of the world”: we was already chosen before the foundation of the world. “That we should be holy and without blame before him in love”: walking in holiness, behaviour as becometh holiness, blameless, walking before him in love.

“Having predestinated us.” The Lord has predestinated us. Ain’t no point of us walking around here acting depressed, acting like we got so much turmoil, ‘Oh, I can’t take it, I can’t go through it.’ The Lord said you already been predestinated, you already been called, you already got a seat in a heavenly place. All you got to do is fulfill your purpose on this earth: put your hand to the plow.

He predestinated us “unto the adoption of children by Jesus Christ to himself, according to the good pleasure of his will.” It’s God’s pleasure to bless you, brothers and sisters in his truth, to raise you up out of the dunghill and set you amongst princes. “To the praise of the glory of his grace, wherein he hath made us accepted in the beloved. In whom we have redemption through his blood, the forgiveness of sins”: we got redemption through his blood, and we’ve been forgiven for the evil we’ve been doing.

“Wherein he hath abounded toward us in all wisdom and prudence; having made known unto us the mystery of his will.” Now you understand you an Israelite, now you understand you got to keep the commandments, now you understand you got a purpose, “according to his good pleasure which he hath purposed in himself.”

“In whom also we have obtained an inheritance, being predestinated according to the purpose of him who worketh all things after the counsel of his own will.” We were predestinated according to his purpose: the same calling “according to his purpose” of Romans 8:28.

“That in the dispensation of the fulness of times he might gather together in one all things in Christ, both which are in heaven, and which are on earth; even in him.” Everything is going to be gathered in one to Christ, everything in heaven and on earth.

That’s why he predestinated us, and that’s our job. We go out here, we teach Christ, we exalt Christ, we let them know: ‘Christ died for your sins. Repent, you’re an Israelite, keep the commandments.’ And our people are going to come back to the understanding.

“I will make a man more precious than fine gold.” When you done fulfilled your purpose, when you finish your course, you going to walk into that gold standard; you going to become that gold the Bible is talking about.

That’s why we get on the brothers about getting a job, about being blameless. Set your finances in order, set your house in order, get your behind in shape, lose the weight, be blameless. Groom yourself, look good, get your line up, keep your hair tight. Walk orderly: don’t be walking through here with holes in your shirt, holes in your pants, busted shoes. If you need help, brothers can help you. We are meant to look like and personify gold. That’s what the Bible says.

“And at that time shall Michael stand up, the great prince which standeth for the children of thy people”: he stands for the children of God’s people, the Israelites. “And there shall be a time of trouble, such as never was since there was a nation even to that same time: and at that time thy people shall be delivered, every one that shall be found written in the book.” If your name is written in the book, brothers, that means you fulfilled your purpose. That’s why your name is in the book: you fulfilled what was predestinated for you.

“And many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life”: those that rise up to everlasting life fulfilled their purpose while they lived. “And some to shame and everlasting contempt”: those that wake up to shame and everlasting contempt did not fulfill their purpose. Their purpose was to keep the commandments; that’s the whole duty of man, and they didn’t fulfill it.

“And they that be wise shall shine as the brightness of the firmament; and they that turn many to righteousness as the stars for ever and ever.” So you brothers out here teaching the gospel, the Bible says you going to shine as the stars for ever and ever. You going to be illuminated; that’s why he says gold, a golden wedge. You going to shine for real, the illumination going to come from you. But you got to remember: you got to fulfill your purpose.

“I have fought a good fight, I have finished my course”: he fulfilled his purpose. The Apostle Paul said, I finished my course, I fulfilled my purpose. “I have kept the faith”: the entire time he kept the faith, until the end.

“Henceforth there is laid up for me a crown of righteousness, which the Lord, the righteous judge, shall give me at that day: and not to me only, but unto all them also that love his appearing.”

Brothers and sisters, that right there is our calling, that’s our purpose. We must finish our course, we must keep the faith, and there’s going to be a crown of righteousness laid up for us. That’s the promise God gave us. It’s time for us to fulfill that purpose.
